includedPullRequests.title: [Part 1/n] Logging Rework: Durable logs, One-tap Export, Log Messages Cleanup
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary This PR is part 1 of many of a major rework of Trio's log handling. It replaces Trio's single text log file with structured, persisted logs for the app, devices and Apple Watch, and a simple export users can actually find and send. ## For users - **Settings → Support & Community → Report a Problem** - **Share Trio Logs:** All Logs, Pump Logs or CGM Logs, for the last 24 hours, 3 days or 7 days. You get one zip with one time-sorted text file. - **Open a GitHub Issue** - **Ask on Discord / Ask on Facebook** stay in the Support & Community section. - **Share Pump Logs / Share CGM Logs** on the pump and CGM screens. - **Exports are redacted.** Nightscout URL and secret, tokens, emails, pump and CGM serials, Bluetooth names and pairing keys are replaced with placeholders. Glucose, insulin, carbs and settings stay in. ## Screenshots | Settings | Submenu | Sheet 1 | Sheet 2 | |--------|--------|--------|--------| | | | | | ## Under the hood - **Device log:** LoopKit's `PersistentDeviceLog` is now actually used. Both delegates forward the manager, device, entry type and message. Kits that forward their whole debug log (Dana, Medtrum, Eversense, AccuChek) are now captured completely. - **App log:** - Free functions route through `os.Logger` plus an async sink, with no lock and no I/O on the caller. - `error` no longer crashes. - Records go to a separate Core Data store (`Documents/logs/AppLog.sqlite`) with levels, categories, ms timestamps and a launch ID. - Retention is by age and by row cap. - **Apple Watch:** - Structured entries with levels and categories, kept in a persistent ring on the watch. - Sent to the phone as OS-queued files with sequence numbers. The phone acknowledges only after storing them. - Exports first ask the watch for fresh entries. - **Both stores are hardened:** - Store creation is deferred until protected data is available, so there's no crash on a background launch before first unlock. - Read-only or corrupt stores are moved aside, and logging falls back to memory. - Bad strings no longer drop whole batches. - **Messages:** - All ~700 call sites rewritten to plain sentences: no emoji, no object dumps, `print`/`debugPrint` removed. - 18 subject-based categories (loop, pump, cgm, nightscout, …). - Every swallowed error is now logged at `warning` or above with the error attached. - Logging guidelines added to `CONTRIBUTING.md`. - **Redaction:** Sensitive elements of logs such as URLs, tokens or Ids are redacted. --- Address: #272, #1633, #1634

includedPullRequests.title: [Part 2/n] Logging Rework: Add "Send to the Trio Team" Reporting Feature
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary This PR builds on #1660 , and adds a private in-app problem report: users describe the problem, add screenshots and their logs, and send it straight to the Trio team. ## For users - **Settings → Support & Community → Report a Problem → Send to the Trio Team** - A description (required), an optional title and up to 8 screenshots or photos. - **Attach My Logs** (on by default): the last 3 days of All Logs, redacted as in Part 1. Glucose, insulin, carbs and settings stay in. - **Contact**: anonymous by default. Users can add a name, email, Discord or GitHub name so the team can follow up. - **Also Sent** shows the exact app version, build, iPhone model, iOS version, pump and CGM that go with the report. - The draft is kept until the report is sent, so a failed send can be retried without retyping. - After sending, users get a report ID (`TR-XXXX-XXXX`) to mention on Discord or Facebook. - **Sent Reports** lists the user's reports from the last 90 days. Each one can be deleted from the server at any time. - Screenshots are re-encoded without location or camera metadata. ## Screenshots | Send Report Form | Send Report Form | Send Report Overview | |--------|--------|--------| | | | | ## For testers Reports go to the production server (`support.triodocs.org`) by default. To send test reports to the dev server instead, add the `TRIO_REPORT_DEV` flag to your `ConfigOverride.xcconfig` (keep any flags you already set there) and rebuild: ``` SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS = $(inherited) TRIO_REPORT_DEV ``` - Works in Debug and Release builds, and for every launch: from the Home Screen, after a restart or a force-quit. - Remove `TRIO_REPORT_DEV` and rebuild to go back to production. - Please mark test reports clearly (e.g. title `Test report, please delete`) and leave out real health details. - The first send after a quiet period can take up to about 30 s while the server wakes up. ## Under the hood - **App Attest client** (`AppAttestClient`) extracted from `TelemetryAttestor` and shared by telemetry and reports. Telemetry keeps its wire format, field names and Keychain entries. Reports use their own key namespace. - **Three-step upload:** 1. A signed `POST /v1/reports` sends text, context and a manifest (name, type, size, SHA-256). 2. Each file goes straight to object storage with a presigned `PUT`, using exactly the headers the server returned. Each file is tried up to 3 times. 3. A signed `complete` call finishes the report. - **Signing:** every signed request uses a fresh challenge. A rejected assertion is retried once. Only an unknown key triggers re-attestation, because reports belong to the key that created them. - **Server:** production (`https://support.triodocs.org`) unless the `TRIO_REPORT_DEV` compilation condition is set, like `DEV_BRANCH_WARNING_DISABLED`, via `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS` in `ConfigOverride.xcconfig`. It only selects the known dev server, never a URL. - DEBUG builds launched from Xcode can also use `-TrioReportDev YES`, or `-TrioReportBaseURL ` for any server. These only apply to the process Xcode starts. - Dev uses its own Keychain namespace (`ReportAttest.dev`), so switching servers never mixes App Attest keys. - DEBUG builds on a simulator use a mock submitter. - **Matches the deployed backend:** - Missing build info is sent as `unknown`. - Title, description and contact limits are counted in Unicode code points, as the server counts them. - Challenge, register and signed calls wait up to 60 s and retry once after a timeout, because the dev server scales to zero. - **Sent reports** are stored locally as ID and date only, and dropped after 90 days to match server retention. - **Error handling:** errors are mapped to plain sentences. - Rate limit, app not allowed (403), too large and unsupported type each get their own message. - On `uploads_incomplete`, Trio uploads the named files once more and completes again. - For other 400 responses, Trio shows the server's own sentence. - "Try Again" appears only where a retry can help. ## Testing - New and updated suites: `ReportClientTests` (26), `ReportProblemTests` (8) and `LogExportTests` all pass. They cover: - signed request shape and hashes - presigned headers - re-attest and assertion retries - cold-server timeouts - incomplete-upload retry - error mapping - limits and code-point counting - `unknown` build info - endpoint selection - drafts and sent reports - The full `Trio Tests` suite passed (960 tests) before the final Part 1 fixes; the report, export, logger and store suites (65 tests) were rerun on the final branch and pass. A SwiftFormat build is clean. - **Sent from an iPhone 15 Pro (iOS 26.6.1) to dev:** a Debug build with `-TrioReportDev YES` registered a new App Attest key (about 3 s) and sent a report with two attachments (about 8 s, mostly the server waking up).

includedPullRequests.title: Bump upload-artifact to v6 in unit tests
includedPullRequests.body:
`actions/upload-artifact@v4` still declares Node 20, so every failed unit-test run shows the "Node.js 20 is deprecated … being forced to run on Node.js 24" warning. v6 declares Node 24 and is what `build_trio.yml` already uses.

- `unit_tests.yml`: both "Upload build log" and "Upload test log" steps now use `actions/upload-artifact@v6`. Inputs (`name`, `path`) are unchanged.
- All other actions in our workflows already run on Node 24, except `actions/add-to-project@v1.0.2` in the disabled `add_to_project.yml` (v2.0.0 runs on Node 24 with the same inputs, left for a separate change).

includedPullRequests.title: Update submodules to current upstream
includedPullRequests.body:
Syncs the loopandlearn forks to their upstreams and bumps the three pins that moved. No other changes.

**EversenseKit** `e7a1850` → `94dc675` (bastiaanv/EversenseKit dev)
Sends `sensorStart` once per sensor instead of once per transmitter setup. State migrates the old `hasReportedInsertionDate` flag to the current sensor.

**MedtrumKit** `c336995` → `41a8202` (jbr7rr/MedtrumKit dev)
Patch-change delivery state (a kept session marker, one suspend per session, retried activation keeps a suspended patch suspended), base-reset detection with a new alert, peripheral re-fetch after a Bluetooth reset, unsaved patch settings kept on sync, and reworked activation/priming instruction screens.

**LoopAlgorithm** `7ef6724` → `e3f5e3c` (LoopKit/LoopAlgorithm main)
Manual glucose entries left out of momentum, ICE and the RC smoothness gate; fixes inverted time factors in mixed glucose/time unit conversions; adds opt-in algorithm experiments, off by default. Trio does not import LoopAlgorithm and none of the changed APIs are used downstream — the new protocol requirements carry extension defaults, so nothing breaks.

Legacy-LoopKit compat is intact: no new async or alert APIs in either device kit, and the existing `issueAlert(_:)` call sites are unchanged.

Everything else is already at the tip of its tracked branch, and every other fork is identical to its upstream.
